name: markdown-link-validity
question: Do all internal markdown links in tracked documentation files resolve to existing targets?

assertion.asserts: every internal markdown citation in the scanned docs names a real target, so a reader following it lands somewhere
assertion.measures: for each [text](dest) outside fenced code and inline code spans, whether the path resolved against the CITING FILE's directory exists in the WORKING TREE right now
known_gaps: working tree, not HEAD: an UNCOMMITTED deletion of a tracked target would make a correct citation look broken -- handled, not accepted (OVALID-05): such targets are classified into the informational uncommitted_deletions bucket and do not set status; commit the deletion and the path leaves that set and fails for real. The gate is deferred, not weakened
resolution is citing-file-relative only: a repo-root-relative citation written without the relative prefix resolves to the wrong path and is reported broken. Cite relative to the citing file
existence, not correctness: a target that exists but no longer contains what the citing sentence claims passes. This oracle cannot see content
anchors are not verified: the #fragment is stripped before resolution, so a citation of a heading that no longer exists passes

markdown link syntax only: bare or backticked paths in prose are never checked, and neither are non-.md files' contents. This is deliberate -- it is what keeps the oracle structurally immune to the manifest-path-value false-positive class (see oracles/README.md)
scope is config.scan_directories + config.scan_root_files: a citation in an unscanned directory is invisible, not passing

cost_provenance: measured 2026-06-12 on the ULDF framework repo under Git Bash (win32; slowest supported environment) -- pessimistic-honest per ORACLE-COST-01; under-declaration causes timeout kills

broken.source: string (path to markdown file containing the broken link)
broken.link: string (the link destination as written, including any anchor)
broken.resolved_path: string (the absolute-from-repo-root path the link was checked against)

details.uncommitted_deletion_count: integer (OVALID-05: citations whose target is tracked and present in HEAD, absent from the working tree only because of an UNCOMMITTED deletion -- informational, never sets status)

uncommitted_deletions.source: string (path to markdown file containing the citation)
uncommitted_deletions.resolved_path: string (the path checked; present in HEAD, deleted-but-uncommitted in the tree)

fallback: Manually grep markdown files for links of the form [text](path), filter out http/https/mailto/tel and bare anchors, then test each resolved path with test -f or Test-Path. Slow and error-prone vs. the oracle.

provenance.note: Starter Verification Oracle for the Verification Oracle category. Dogfoods the category by validating ULDF's own internal documentation links. v1.1.0 (2026-07-20): the manifest declared validate.{sh,ps1} self-tests the directory never shipped -- authored them (5 anti-silent-breakage cases: clean tree, one-broken, exclusions, relative-nesting, empty-scope). Writing them surfaced a latent run.ps1 defect: an `[ordered]@{...}` literal with an array-valued entry threw ArgumentException on Windows PowerShell 5.1 (the framework's primary Windows shell), so the Windows path emitted nothing and silently exited 0 -- fixed by materializing broken[] with List.ToArray() and building the maps incrementally. v1.2.0 (2026-07-30, OVALID-05/DEC-220): this oracle was the framework's own instance of the DEFER-044 asserts-P/measures-Q class -- it asserted 'the citation resolves' and measured working-tree presence, so a live sibling session's UNCOMMITTED deletion of a target present in HEAD reddened it with the citation entirely correct (reproduced in an isolated repo before the fix). Added the informational uncommitted_deletions bucket via git ls-files --deleted plus the textual path canonicalization the comparison needs (git never emits `..` segments; the oracle resolves citing-file-relative and does), and the assertion declaration above. Self-tests gained T6a/T6b/T6c; both were demonstrated RED against a blanket-amnesty mutant and against a neutered canonicalizer.

config.comment: Edit scan_directories or scan_root_files to change scope. Avoid adding huge directories: this oracle has a <2s speed contract.
